strings.foot.a: Which measure a number belongs to is stated inside each item: sections 1 and 2 use all-cause or cause-specific mortality, sections 3 and 4 energy and time, section 5 money, section 7 money and benefits, sections 8 and 9 money and personal freedom. They are not converted into each other. The verification trail is in
strings.foot.c: . Credit the author and link the original if you reprint or adapt it.
strings.gloss.note: Underlined terms in the text explain themselves when you click one or hover over it. The full table is below.
strings.head.p1: Every item answers two questions: what it costs, and what it buys back.
strings.head.p2: Who benefits is graded too: you first, then your spouse and immediate family, then friends and colleagues, strangers last. Last does not mean zero — only that the return is unlikely, and that you have to weigh the risks along with it.
strings.head.p3: You do not have to do all of it. This is a shortlist ordered by value for money, not a task list. Taking one or two entries with you counts; come back for the rest when you need them. For the cheapest ones, set "Money spent" to "No money" and "Willpower needed" to "No willpower" on the left. The author has not done most of them either. Dotted "item X" references in the text open in place, so you can see what that item says without hunting for it.
strings.hint.p1: One section at a time; costs and grades can take several values. Several values inside one group are "or"; different groups are "and".
strings.hint.p2: Items are ordered from best to worst value within each section. Searching does not change the order.

strings.meta.description: A life guide ordered by value for money: {{entries}} pieces of advice on longevity and disease prevention, accident first aid, saving money, scams and legal red lines, income support, business risk, dating and marriage, going abroad, and skills. Each one states its cost, its benefit, the grade of evidence, and the original sources, and you can filter by the three costs of money, time, and willpower.

strings.noscript.p1: Get back the most lifespan, money and personal freedom for the least money, time, energy and willpower. {{sections}} sections, {{entries}} items, each stating its cost, benefit, evidence grade and original sources. Benefits are graded by who receives them: you, your spouse and immediate family, friends and colleagues, strangers — the lower the grade, the smaller the expected return and the more the risks have to be spelled out.
